title: App page
summary: An authenticated app dashboard composed from the app shell, sidebar navigation, KPI stats, and a data-table view.
brief: Build a logged-in app screen: an AppShell frame wrapping an AppSidebarNav in the sidebar slot, with the main region holding a row of AppStats KPIs above an AppDataTable list. Keep page content in Server Components and pass it as the shell's children; only the shell and any interactive controls are client-side. Use semantic tokens so the whole app restyles with the theme.

sections.intent: The outer frame — fixed sidebar, sticky top bar, scrollable main.
Primary navigation inside the shell's sidebar slot.
Headline KPIs at the top of the main region.
The primary list/table view below the stats.

layout: AppShell is the root. Put AppSidebarNav in its `sidebar` slot and page title + actions in its `header` slot. Inside `children`, stack AppStats first, then AppDataTable. For a settings screen, swap AppDataTable for app-settings. Each block manages its own spacing — separate stacked blocks with a gap on the main region. Each section installs as its own file — import a block from `@/components/ui/<section.block>` (e.g. import { AppShell } from "@/components/ui/app-shell").

checklist.check: [AppShell] Avoid: Rendering the whole page as a Client Component because AppShell is one — keep page content in Server Components and pass it as children.
[AppShell] Avoid: Duplicating navigation in both the sidebar and the header — the sidebar is the primary nav.
[AppShell] Avoid: Forgetting to give the sidebar a scroll region when the nav is long — AppSidebarNav handles this; raw content may overflow.

[AppShell] A11y: The mobile menu button is a <button> with aria-expanded and an aria-label. The drawer backdrop is a labelled button so it's keyboard-dismissable. The sticky top bar stays above content via z-index without trapping focus.
[AppSidebarNav] Avoid: Marking multiple items active — only the current page should have active=true (it sets aria-current='page').
[AppSidebarNav] Avoid: Passing an as an item icon — the icon slot is sized for a glyph (size-4); use an SVG.
[AppSidebarNav] Avoid: Putting more than ~3 groups with long lists without scannable titles — title each group.

[AppSidebarNav] A11y: Links are real anchors; the active link carries aria-current='page'. Icons are aria-hidden since the adjacent label conveys meaning. The nav region scrolls independently so the brand and footer stay visible.
[AppStats] Avoid: Relying on color alone for increase/decrease — the caret direction and the sign in the change text both encode it, so keep the sign (e.g. '-0.3%').
[AppStats] Avoid: Setting changeType='increase' for a metric where down is good (e.g. churn) — pick the type by sentiment, not arithmetic.
[AppStats] Avoid: Mismatched columns and stat count, leaving a ragged row.
[AppStats] A11y: Deltas don't rely on color alone: a directional caret plus the signed change text convey direction. Carets are aria-hidden. Values and labels are plain text, read in source order.
[AppDataTable] Avoid: Expecting sorting/filtering from this block — it's layout; that logic lives in the DataTable you pass as children.
[AppDataTable] Avoid: Putting the page <h1> here when AppShell's header already has one — this title is a section <h2>.
[AppDataTable] Avoid: Omitting a footer with pagination on long tables, leaving no way to page.

[AppDataTable] A11y: The section title renders as an <h2>. The block doesn't add table semantics — those come from the Table/DataTable in children. Toolbar controls should carry their own labels (e.g. a search input with an accessible name).
